transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I'd like to call this review session to order regarding the medication-safety simulation assessment plan for this term. As we all know, we have 12 students who need to complete this assessment, and the draft plan on the table uses a faculty evaluator, two rotations of six students, an assessment date of May 8, 2027, and a results-entry date of June 21, 2027. Before I can give my final approval, we need to go through our standard round-robin review. I'd like to hear from each of you in turn — the clinical coordinator, simulation-lab manager, registrar, and student-services coordinator. Please share your reports on the draft, and I'll record each one before we settle the plan. Who would like to begin?

transcript.text: I'd like to begin with my report. During this month's clinical-compliance review, I confirmed that the state nursing board's current medication-simulation rule requires the evaluator to be a current, unencumbered registered nurse. However, the draft plan currently specifies only 'faculty evaluator' without stating this credential requirement. This needs to be corrected before the plan can be approved.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I'd like to give my report as simulation-lab manager. I completed the equipment check yesterday, and I need to flag a critical issue: only three of our medication pumps currently have valid calibration certificates. Our lab safety procedure limits each pump rotation to a maximum of three students. The draft plan calls for two rotations of six students, but with only three calibrated pumps available, each rotation can safely accommodate no more than three students. This means the rotation count needs to be revised before the plan can be approved.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I'd like to give my report as registrar. During my review this week, I verified the date against the registrar's accreditation calendar, and I need to flag a critical issue: the program's accreditation calendar requires all results to be entered by June 14, 2027. However, the draft plan still carries a results-entry date of June 21, 2027, which is one week past the accreditation deadline. This needs to be corrected before the plan can be approved.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I'd like to give my report as student-services coordinator. During my review, I found that two enrolled students have approved religious-observance absences on May 8, 2027 — the current assessment date in the draft. I've reviewed their approved notices and family confirmations, and both students have confirmed that May 10, 2027 is an available assessment date for them. The draft plan has not yet been updated to account for these absences, so the assessment date needs to be revised before the plan can be approved.
